segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Karen. I pulled up the quote in the CRM. We’ve got 42 user seats, the implementation package, and the reporting add-on, with a target go-live of September 16.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That matches what I have. The only thing I wanted to double-check is the seat count. We may need 45, but three of those would be read-only managers.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, so the pricing sheet has read-only seats at $18 per user per month, versus $64 for full users. If we change it to 42 full and 3 read-only, the annual total comes to $34,848 before tax.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, that’s within the range finance approved. Can you also confirm the invoice timing? We need the first invoice after July 1, not before.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Absolutely. I’ll set the billing start date as July 1 in the billing tool, net 30 terms. So the invoice would generate July 1 and be due July 31.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. And implementation is still four weeks? Our ops team wants training done before Labor Day.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Correct. If we get signature by June 21, kickoff would be June 26, configuration in July, user training the week of August 19, and then go-live September 16. There’s a little buffer in there.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. On the contract, our legal team asked for a one-year term with a 60-day renewal notice. Is that in the draft?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: It is now. I updated the order form to a 12-month initial term and 60 days’ notice before renewal. I’ll send that through deal desk today for the standard review.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send me the revised quote and order form, and I’ll route it to procurement this afternoon.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. You’ll have the revised documents by 2:00 Eastern, and I’ll include the implementation timeline in the email so procurement has everything in one place.
